- Model tends to overestimate prices in early periods of the 30-day forecast, especially after recent spikes.
- Forecast often peaks too early and then declines too sharply, missing sustained upward momentum.
- Model underestimates true outcomes in the middle-to-late portion of the forecast horizon, particularly after a spike.
- Model shows persistent bias toward lower values in the final 5–10 days of the forecast, suggesting mean reversion or lagged adjustment.
- Overshoots after sharp price increases (e.g., 60→64) are common, followed by a correction that underestimates the true decline.
- Model fails to capture the “late surge” effect — true prices often rise again after a dip, but model predicts a flat or downward trend.
- Forecast exhibits lagged response to recent price movements — e.g., a 5-day spike is not fully reflected in the 30-day forecast until later days.
- Model tends to underestimate the true mean of the 30-day window, especially when the true outcome is trending upward.
